chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
title: Witness in the Pennsylvania trial: lawyers friendly in the judge's chambers
summary: Called to testify for two years, he is surprised that the prosecutor, defense lawyer and judge chat like old friends.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I was called later, for the next two years, to come up to the little town in Pennsylvania near where this happened, to trial, to be a witness. I was called up there by the State's Attorney. And in being a witness I learned something about the courts. When they had me up there, they paid me a small sum of money, and I had a hotel room and everything. On the day of the trial, I would sit back in the judge's chambers until everything was ready. Sitting back there, I was... I can't remember the name of this little town. But the district attorney, who had me up, would be back there, and all of a sudden a fellow would walk in and he would say something to

the fact of "Hi, Tom, how's the wife and kids?" "Oh, fine." And they'd have a conversation. "What have you been doing?" "Oh, I was up and some creek or something the other day. They were really biting up there." And I'm sitting there. "Oh, by the way, this is John Malachi. John, this is Judge So-and-So." And I would meet him... I had never known just what happened in the judge's chambers. After a while, another guy would come in, and I would be introduced to him, and they would have the same kind of conversation, and I would find out that he was the defense lawyer. So I always had this impression, I guess from the movies and television, that these guys were archenemies and that they didn't hardly speak to each other otherwise. But I found out that they were great friends and family friends, etcetera.
